notes.purpose: M17 step 4: how the result moves with the price of leaving a provider and with the number of candidate regions (06 S12).
notes.egress_multipliers: multiplies every CROSS-PROVIDER egress rate; same-provider inter-region rates, the zero diagonal and internet rates are untouched, so the knob is exactly 'what does leaving a provider cost'. x = 1 reproduces the real snapshot exactly and anchors the sweep.
notes.locations_per_provider: prefix of each provider's regions in LOCATIONS_EXT declaration order, so the grids nest: k = 1 subset 2 subset 4 subset 8. k = 4 is exactly the core location set and k = 8 is ext, which ties the sweep to the rest of the project.
notes.location_set: ext, because the k axis needs 8 regions per provider to exist; k = 4 reproduces core.
notes.comparability: these transforms change the true cost model, so a row is comparable only with rows at the same (egress_mult, locs_per_provider). Both are their own runs.csv columns and part of the configuration key in check_replication.
notes.draws: R = 10 (05 S2 default for a grid this size; the n >= 3 floor is what check_replication enforces). Same draw ids and generator as results/replicates, so the grid is paired with the s = 1 core rows.
notes.methods: ilp_full, b1 and b2_best only: the question here is how the OPTIMUM and the baselines move, not which heuristic tracks it.

notes.runs.csv: one row per (instance, method, seed); standard columns (01 §4) first; appended as each job finishes; resume skips present keys.
notes.runtime_s: method wall time; ILP = build + CBC; greedy_1opt includes greedy.
notes.status: optimal (ILP proven) | feasible (ILP incumbent, not proven) | no_solution | ok (heuristic or baseline)
